Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The test `testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode()` fails likely due to issues in handling long directory names and PAX headers in the `TarArchiveOutputStream` class.

From the test, a `TarArchiveEntry` is created with a directory name "föö/" that contains non-ASCII characters. The test sets `setAddPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames(true)` on the `TarArchiveOutputStream` instance, triggering logic to add PAX headers for entries with non-ASCII names.

Looking into `TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry()`, when the entry name is longer than the allowed TAR name length (usually 100 bytes), and if `longFileMode == LONGFILE_POSIX`, a PAX header is created with the entry name added as a "path" attribute. Also, if `addPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames` is enabled and the entry name is non-ASCII, the code again adds the "path" attribute to the PAX headers.

These PAX headers are then written by `writePaxHeaders()`. This method creates a PAX header entry that has a name starting with "./PaxHeaders.X/" followed by a sanitized version of the original entry name. Problematic is that if this resulting PAX header entry name is longer than the TAR `NAMELEN` (100 bytes), it is truncated.

The bug report mentions an exception while writing PAX headers related to directory names longer than 100 bytes, where the size in header is 0 but an attempt is made to write a larger number of bytes, causing an `IOException`.

This problem is likely to result from the truncation in `writePaxHeaders` of the PAX header entry name. The truncation is done blindly to fit the name within `NAMELEN - 1` bytes. Thus, for long directory names, the path for the PAX header entry may be truncated, leading to the mismatch between the size declared in the header and the actual data size. This inconsistency triggers the exception about writing more bytes than expected.

In summary, the method that sets the PAX header entry name truncates the path too aggressively without ensuring consistency between the header size and the actual data size written. The test fails with a non-ASCII directory name scenario that triggers PAX header usage and the truncation bug. 

This diagnosis aligns with the current bug report's symptom of long directory names causing exceptions with PAX headers.

Recent bug reports about long entry names, encoding, and PAX headers further support that the problem is about handling names and headers correctly when dealing with long or non-ASCII entry names.

Hence, the root cause is the improper handling of the PAX header entry name length and size consistency in `TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders`.

Next, I can suggest fixes focusing on `putArchiveEntry` and `writePaxHeaders`.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode()` exercises adding a non-ASCII directory name entry to a tar archive using POSIX PAX headers. The test triggers the code path in `TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry` where PAX headers are added for long or non-ASCII names. The method `writePaxHeaders` creates a PAX header entry named "./PaxHeaders.X/" plus a sanitized version of the original entry name, but if this name exceeds the TAR maximum name length (100 bytes), it is truncated to fit. This truncation leads to a mismatch between the PAX header entry size (set based on untruncated data length) and the actual PAX header entry name length in the TAR header. This inconsistency causes an IOException when writing PAX header contents due to the archive expecting fewer bytes than are written. The current bug report and test suggest that this truncation of the PAX header entry name without ensuring size consistency for long directory names causes the failure. Recent related bug reports about long file names and PAX header handling reinforce the conclusion that the bug lies in the handling of PAX header entry names and sizes in `TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
